{{Short description|Physicist}}
'''Malvin Carl Teich''' is an American electrical engineer, physicist, and computational neuroscientist which is professor emeritus of electrical engineering at [[Columbia University]] and physics at [[Boston University]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Malvin Carl Teich | website=IEEE Xplore | url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37270634400 | access-date=February 17, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Personal Website |url=https://people.bu.edu/teich/index.html|website=Boston University |access-date= 4 November 2021|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20211026153234/https://people.bu.edu/teich/index.html | url-status=live| archive-date=26 October 2021}}</ref> He is also a consultant to government, academia, and private industry, where he serves as an advisor in [[Intellectual property|intellectual-property]] conflicts. He is the coauthor of ''Fundamentals of Photonics'' (Wiley, 3rd Ed. 2019, with B. E. A. Saleh),<ref name = "FOP">{{cite book |last1=Saleh |first1=Bahaa E. A. |last2=Teich |first2=Malvin Carl |title=Fundamentals of Photonics |date=2019 |publisher=Wiley |location=Hoboken, N.J. |isbn=978-1-119-50687-4 |edition=Third |ref=FOP}}</ref> and of ''Fractal-Based Point Processes'' (Wiley, 2005, with S. B. Lowen).<ref name = "FBPP">{{cite book |last1=Lowen |first1=Steven Bradley |last2=Teich |first2=Malvin Carl |title=Fractal-Based Point Processes |date=2005 |publisher=Wiley-Interscience |location=Hoboken, N.J. |isbn=978-0-471-38376-5 |ref=FBPP}}</ref>

==Education==
Teich's academic credentials include an S.B. degree in physics from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], an M.S. degree in electrical engineering from [[Stanford University]], and a Ph.D. degree from [[Cornell University]]. His bachelor's thesis, written jointly with Paul J. Schweitzer and supervised by Theos J. Thompson, investigated the total neutron cross section of [[palladium]] using the fast chopper at the [[MIT Nuclear Research Reactor|M.I.T. nuclear reactor]].<ref>{{cite thesis |type= S.B. |oclc= 33098348 |last1=Schweitzer |first1=Paul Jerome |last2=Teich |first2=Malvin Carl |title=The Total Neutron Cross Section of Palladium Using the M.I.T. Fast Chopper |publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Department of Physics |url = https://people.bu.edu/teich/pdfs/Thesis-SB-1961-Teich.pdf |access-date= 7 November 2021 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20211107184745/https://people.bu.edu/teich/pdfs/Thesis-SB-1961-Teich.pdf| url-status=live| archive-date=7 November 2021 |date=June 1961}}</ref> In carrying out his Ph.D. dissertation, supervised by George J. Wolga, he made use of the then-new [[Gallium arsenide|gallium-arsenide]] [[laser diode]] to observe the nonlinear two-photon [[photoelectric effect]] in metallic [[sodium]].<ref>{{cite thesis |type=Ph.D. |oclc= 703779359|last1=Teich |first1=Malvin Carl |title=Two Quantum Photoemission and dc Photomixing in Sodium |url= https://people.bu.edu/teich/pdfs/Thesis-PhD-1966-Teich.pdf|publisher=Cornell University |access-date=10 October 2021|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20210912214104/http://people.bu.edu/teich/pdfs/Thesis-PhD-1966-Teich.pdf | url-status=live| archive-date=12 September 2021 |date=February 1966}}</ref> The principal results that followed from his doctoral dissertation were published in [[Physical Review Letters]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Teich |first1=M. C. |last2=Schroeer |first2=J. M. |last3=Wolga |first3=G. J. |title=Double-Quantum Photoelectric Emission from Sodium Metal |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=23 November 1964 |volume=13 |issue=21 |pages=611–614 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.611|bibcode=1964PhRvL..13..611T }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Teich |first1=M. C. |last2=Wolga |first2=G. J. |title=Multiple-Photon Processes and Higher Order Correlation Functions |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=4 April 1966 |volume=16 |issue=14 |pages=625–628 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.16.625|bibcode=1966PhRvL..16..625T }}</ref>

==Career==
Teich assumed his first professional affiliation in January 1966 at [[M.I.T. Lincoln Laboratory]], as a member of the research group directed by Robert J. Keyes and Robert H. Kingston. In September 1967, he joined the faculty of  [[Columbia University]], where he served as a member of the Electrical Engineering Department (as Chairman from 1978 to 1980), the Applied Physics and Applied Mathematics Department, the Columbia Radiation Laboratory (founded and directed by [[Isidor Isaac Rabi|I. I. Rabi]]) in the Department of Physics, and the Fowler Memorial Laboratory (directed by Shyam M. Khanna) in the Department of Otolaryngology at the [[Columbia University_Irving_Medical_Center |Columbia University Medical Center]]. In 1996, he was appointed Professor Emeritus of Engineering Science and Applied Physics.<ref>{{cite web |title= Professor Emeritus in Columbia University|url= https://www.ee.columbia.edu/people/all|website= Department of Electrical Engineering |access-date= 4 November 2021|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20210607000732/https://www.ee.columbia.edu/people/all | url-status=live| archive-date=7 June 2021}}</ref> In 1995, concurrently with his Emeritus status at Columbia, he joined [[Boston University]] as a faculty member in the Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering (as Director of the Quantum Photonics Laboratory and as a member of the [[Boston University Photonics Center]]), the Department of Biomedical Engineering (as a member of the Graduate Program for Neuroscience and the Hearing Research Center), and the Department of Physics. In 2011, he was appointed Professor Emeritus of Electrical & Computer Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, and Physics in Boston University.<ref>Professor Emeritus in Boston University:
* {{cite web |title= Faculty Directory |url=https://www.bu.edu/eng/departments/ece/people/|website= Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering |access-date= 4 November 2021|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20211106214944/https://www.bu.edu/eng/departments/ece/people/| url-status=live| archive-date=6 November 2021}}
* {{cite web |title= Faculty Directory |url=https://www.bu.edu/eng/departments/bme/people/|website= Department of Biomedical Engineering |access-date= 5 November 2021|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20211105170107/https://www.bu.edu/eng/departments/bme/people/| url-status=live| archive-date=5 November 2021}}
* {{cite web |title= Faculty Directory |url= https://www.bu.edu/physics/people/emeriti/|website= Department of Physics |access-date= 5 November 2021|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20211020063244/https://www.bu.edu/physics/people/emeriti/| url-status=live| archive-date=20 October 2021}}</ref> Over the course of his career, his efforts in quantum photonics have been devoted to exploring the properties, behavior, and applications of classical and nonclassical light, including its generation, characterization, modulation, transmission, propagation, amplification, detection, and frequency-conversion. In computational neuroscience, he has concentrated on elucidating the role of fractal stochastic processes in neural information transmission. He has also worked on codifying the detection laws of audition and vision, an enterprise that lies at the interface of [[Photonics|quantum photonics]] and [[computational neuroscience]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bahar |first1=Sonya |title=A Conversation with Mal Teich |journal=The Biological Physicist |date=October 2005 |volume=5 |issue=4 |page=1-5 |url=https://people.bu.edu/teich/pdfs/BiolPhysicist-5-4-1-2005.pdf |access-date=25 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211225212427/https://people.bu.edu/teich/pdfs/BiolPhysicist-5-4-1-2005.pdf |archive-date=25 December 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Teich |first1=M. C. |title=Paul R. Prucnal and Bhavin J. Shastri, Neuromorphic Photonics. |date=2017 |publisher=CRC Press |location=Boca Raton |isbn=978-1-4987-2522-4 |pages=xi-xvii |chapter-url=https://people.bu.edu/teich/pdfs/Prucnal-Preface-2017.pdf |access-date=7 November 2021|chapter=Foreword: At the Interface of Photonics and Neuroscience |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20211106203449/https://people.bu.edu/teich/pdfs/Prucnal-Preface-2017.pdf| url-status=live| archive-date=6 November 2021}}</ref>
